'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[ISIL insurgency in Iraq (2017–present)|ISIL insurgency in Iraq]]
**At least four people are killed and 17 others are wounded in a [[car bomb]] attack at a market in [[Sadr City]], [[Baghdad]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/4/15/car-bomb-kills-four-in-baghdads-sadr-city-say-police (Al Jazeera)]
*[[2021 Myanmar protests]]
**Security forces arrest 25-year-old Wai Moe Naing, one of the most prominent leaders of the anti-[[2021 Myanmar coup d'état|coup]] protests, near [[Monywa]]. Separately, [[Tatmadaw|soldiers]] open fire on protesters in [[Mandalay]] to disperse a group of medical workers, killing one person and injuring several others. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-myanmar-politics/myanmar-security-forces-arrest-prominent-leader-of-campaign-against-coup-idUSKBN2C20CJ (Reuters)]
*[[Gaza–Israel conflict]]
**[[Israeli Air Force]] jets and helicopters strike [[Hamas]]-linked targets in the [[Gaza Strip]] in retaliation for earlier rocket fire targeting southern [[Israel]]. The [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] says that an armaments production facility and a tunnel used to smuggle weapons were hit. [https://www.timesofisrael.com/israel-strikes-hamas-targets-after-gaza-rocket-fire/ (''The Times of Israel'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Divers arrive at the scene of [[lift boat]] [[ship prefix|MV]] ''[[Seacor Power]]'', which capsized and partially sank off the coast of the state of [[Louisiana]] in the United States. [[Search and rescue|Rescuers]] suspect crew members may be trapped. Since the accident, six crew members have been rescued, one has died, and twelve remain missing. [https://www.katc.com/news/covering-louisiana/ntsb-to-assist-coast-guard-in-capsized-boat-investigation (KATC-TV)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] surpasses 10,000 deaths from COVID-19. [https://bdnews24.com/bangladesh/2021/04/15/bangladeshs-covid-death-toll-tops-10000 (Bdnews24.com)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Delhi]]
*****[[Chief Minister of Delhi|Chief Minister]] [[Arvind Kejriwal]] announces a weekend curfew in the national capital territory of [[Delhi]] from 10:00 p.m. on Saturday to 5:00 a.m. on Monday due to a substantial increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://m.economictimes.com/news/india/government-announces-weekend-curfew-in-delhi-to-control-sudden-spike/articleshow/82080878.cms (''The Economic Times'')]
****[[India]] reports a record 200,739 new cases and 1,038 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to over 14 million and confirmed deaths to 173,123. India is also the second country to surpass 14 million cases, after the [[United States]]. [https://apnews.com/article/migrant-workers-mumbai-weddings-india-coronavirus-pandemic-766287564341fc7b4281b208bfdad630 (AP)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Philippines]]
****The [[Philippines]] surpasses 900,000 total cases of COVID-19. [https://news.abs-cbn.com/news/04/15/21/total-covid-19-cases-in-ph-breach-900000-mark-with-11429-new-infections (ABS-CBN News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Thailand]]
****[[Thailand]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 1,543 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 37,453. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/learning/easy/2100147/1-543-new-covid-19-cases-thursday (''Bangkok Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]

****[[President of the European Commission]] [[Ursula von der Leyen]] receives her first dose of the [[Pfizer–BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer–BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://www.politico.eu/article/angela-merkel-ursula-von-der-leyen-coronavirus-vaccine-astrazeneca/ (''Politico'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]

****[[Turkey]] reports a record 297 deaths in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 35,031. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-turkey/turkey-reports-297-deaths-due-to-covid-19-highest-daily-level-yet-ministry-idUSKBN2C22EG (Reuters)]

***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Nunavut]]
****[[Nunavut]]'s capital [[Iqaluit]] imposes a [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] after the first COVID-19 case was reported last night. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/health/coronavirus/iqaluit-locks-down-after-reporting-its-first-covid-19-case-in-pandemic-1.5388898 (CTV News)]

***[[Argentina]]'s president [[Alberto Fernández]] announces that his government is closing schools and imposing a curfew in [[Buenos Aires]] amidst a spike of the COVID-19 cases. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/argentine-president-cleared-following-bout-covid-19-2021-04-15/ (Reuters)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Russia–United States relations]]
**The [[United States]] imposes retaliatory measures against [[Russia]] in response to the [[2020 United States federal government data breach]], [[Russian interference in the 2020 United States elections|its interference in the 2020 United States elections]], and the [[Annexation of Crimea by the Russian Federation|occupation]] of and human rights abuses in [[Crimea]]. The U.S. bans trade in bonds newly issued by Russia's [[Central Bank of Russia|Central Bank]], [[Russian National Wealth Fund|National Wealth Fund]], and [[Ministry of Finance (Russia)|Ministry of Finance]], formally names the [[Russian Foreign Intelligence Service]] as responsible for the data breach, blacklists 32 Russian entities and individuals, and expels ten Russian diplomats. Russia denies these allegations. The [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Russia)|Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs]] summons the U.S. ambassador to inform him that "a series of retaliatory measures will follow soon". A spokesperson for the ministry also says that a potential summit between both countries' leaders may not take place. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/14/politics/russia-sanctions-expel-officials-hacking-election/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/us-imposes-wide-array-sanctions-russia-malign-actions-2021-04-15/ (Reuters)]
*[[Russia–Ukraine relations]]
**[[Ukraine]] protests an alleged announcement by [[Russia]] that, beginning next week, it would be closing the [[Kerch Strait]] to foreign warships and state ships until October. [https://interfax.com.ua/news/general/737914-amp.html (Interfax-Ukraine)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Killing of Adam Toledo]]
**The [[Chicago Police Department]] publicly releases [[Body camera|bodycam]] footage of the shooting of 13-year-old [[Mexican American]] boy Adam Toledo. The footage appears to show an unarmed Toledo with both his arms raised in the air before being fatally shot in the chest by an officer. [[Chicago Mayor]] [[Lori Lightfoot]] says "Simply put, we failed Adam" and calls for calm amidst fears of unrest. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-us-canada-56768217 (BBC News)]
**Several protests take place around the city after the video is released, including one that briefly shut down northbound [[Michigan Avenue, Chicago|Michigan Avenue]] and another at [[Union Park (Chicago)|Union Park]]. [https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/release-of-adam-toledo-shooting-video-sparks-protests-emotional-reactions/2487854/ (WMAQ-TV)]
*[[Indianapolis FedEx shooting]]
**Eight people are killed and seven others injured in a [[mass shooting]] at a [[FedEx]] facility in [[Indianapolis]], [[Indiana]], United States. Police say the gunman [[Murder–suicide|took his own life]] afterwards. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/16/us/indianapolis-shooting-fedex-facility/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.cnn.com/2021/04/16/us/what-we-know-indianapolis-fedex-shooting/index.html (CNN<sup>2</sup>)] [https://apnews.com/article/shootings-crime-indianapolis-indiana-e92ad3117c56357b3b2c71a2903e68a8 (AP)]
*Residents of [[Essouassi]], [[Mahdia Governorate]], [[Tunisia]], [[arson|torch]] the local [[police station]], and a police vehicle, after two young men are killed in a traffic accident with a police vehicle. Personnel evacuate the facility, and no one is hurt. [https://www.middleeastmonitor.com/20210415-tunisia-protesters-burn-police-station-after-men-killed-in-car-accident-with-officers/ (Middle East Monitor)]
*The [[Government of France|French]] [[National Assembly (France)|National Assembly]] votes unanimously to amend an existing [[age of consent]] law in order to officially recognize sex with children under the age of 15 as [[rape]] and making it punishable by up to 20 years in prison. Previously, the law allowed an adult to claim the [[sexual consent|consent]] of a child in court. The bill also classifies [[incest]]uous sex with a minor under the age of 18 as rape. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/france-outlaws-sex-with-minors-2021-04-15/ (Reuters)]
*The French National Assembly approves a controversial [[global security law proposal]] that extends police powers and makes it a crime to help identify on-duty police officers "with the obvious intent of harming". [[Amnesty International]] denounces the law's "generalized surveillance practices" and "vague provisions". [https://www.dailysabah.com/world/europe/france-passes-controversial-security-bill-to-extend-police-powers (AP via ''Daily Sabah'')]
